paragraphs: Mia's Butterfly Fact File, posted by Mia. On Saturday, the Explorers spent a morning in the nature park with Ranger Mark. The park was green and quiet. Many flowers were open. Ranger Mark lent each of us a small magnifying glass for looking at insects. I looked at a butterfly on a flower, and I took a photo. The butterfly was orange and black. It did not move for a minute. Then it flew away. Leo said, "That is a wonderful photo of a butterfly in action!" Here is my fact file.

Size: a butterfly is about ten centimeters wide with open wings. It has four wings, and each wing has a pattern. Food: it drinks nectar, the sweet juice of flowers. Home: it lives in gardens, parks, and forests. Butterflies like warm weather, and they rest when it rains. It sees many colors, and it finds flowers by their color. Life: it lives for about two weeks, and possibly for a month. It is a small creature, but it is very important for nature.

A butterfly is not born with wings. First, the mother puts a very small egg on a leaf. After a few days, a caterpillar is born from the egg. The caterpillar is a small, soft insect, and it eats leaves all day. It grows bigger and bigger.

Then the caterpillar stops eating and makes a hard case around its body. It stays inside for about ten days. During this time, its body changes. Then the case opens, and a butterfly comes out. Its wings are wet and soft, so it waits for a few hours. Then the wings are dry, and the butterfly can fly.

I think that a butterfly is a wonderful animal. It begins as a small egg, and it ends with beautiful wings. Leo asked me, "Can you lend me your photo for a poster?" "Of course," I said, "but please give it back." I like gardens with many flowers. I want to see the butterfly again. Which insect do you like best? Tell us in a message!
